text: Right, But we want to paint on the 3d model. not on the atlas. the atlas just is there and the paint is a layer on it, never repainting the atlas
resolution: Built cart/paint_on_3d_demo.tsx — the 3D sequel proving the corrected architecture the user taught: (1) you paint ON the 3D model surface (raycast from cursor finds the face + point), NOT on the atlas; (2) the mesh material (the read-only base atlas) is never touched — the grid+highlight is a separate projected LAYER on top; (3) the grid is UNIFORM in model-surface space (one fixed CELL world-size on every face), so a wide face shows more cells and a thin face fewer, never sliver cells, and the auto-orbit camera ALSO oscillates distance (zoom) to show the grid stays the same size on the surface regardless of zoom; (4) the hovered cell clips per-face and cannot spill across a shared box edge onto the perpendicular neighbour. Grid/highlight projected via meshSelect.makeProjector (replicates gpu/3d.zig) so the overlay sits exactly on the rendered faces; hover polls getMouseX/Y since onMouseMove only fires while a button is held. Verified: base shot shows the uniform grid locked to all 3 visible faces; a forced-hover shot shows the amber cell clipped to the top face at the box edge, not wrapping onto the side.
